extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/arithmetic-geometry and anabelian geometry (readers familiar with IUT/Mochizuki techniques, etale cohomology, log-curves)
extracted.subtask_description: Collects the definitions, structural properties, cohomological identifications, and rigidity/compatibility criteria for the etale theta function, associated torsors/sections, and related constructions in the setting of log-curves and arithmetic fundamental groups (IUT context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical integral structure of Dy
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 7.3: the canonical reduction of the (L^) -torsor Sect(Dy -> G_K) to a canonical O_L-torsor; the L-torsor obtained by push-out via O_L -> L is the canonical discrete structure; the prime-to-p quotient (O_L)_0 is the canonical tame integral structure of Dy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A section s in Sect(Dy -> G_K) is 'compatible with the canonical integral structure of Dy' if s comes from a section of the canonical O_L-torsor. One may further consider reductions of the (L^) -torsor to finite torsors (f_{1}g-structure or (Z/2l)-structure); a section is compatible with such a structure if it comes from a section of the corresponding torsor. The canonical discrete/tame integral structures are obtained by push-out and prime-to-p quotients respectively (see also [AbsSect, Definition 4.1]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero/pole divisor of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 7.4(1): the etale theta function θ := θ((U)) extends uniquely to a meromorphic function on Y; θ has zeroes of order 1 at the cusps of Y and no other zeroes, and θ has poles of order j^2 on the irreducible component labelled j and no other poles (the divisor of poles equals D1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This divisor description follows from the translation formula (Lemma 7.4(2)) and the fact that θ is a regular function on the canonical component U. Checking simple zeroes at U = 1 and reducing modulo the maximal ideal of O_K are used in the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation formulas of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 7.4(2): explicit transformation/translation formulas under actions by a in 2Z and under inversion automorphisms: e.g. θ(U^{(0)1}) = (0)·θ(U) and relations showing how θ behaves under component-index shifts and multiplication-by-squares (these give the translation formula for changing irreducible components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equalities provide the group-theoretic and coordinate-change behavior used to read off zero/pole divisors and to describe how theta classes transform under the action of Z (or 2Z) and inversion automorphisms of the underlying elliptic curve. They are used throughout to compare theta-values on different components (see the displayed equalities in Lemma 7.4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer classes associated to the theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 7.4(3),(4): the cohomology classes O_K(1)(θ) are precisely the Kummer classes associated to an O_K-multiple of the regular function θ on the Raynaud generic fiber of Y. For a non-cuspidal point y in Y(L) (L/K finite) the restriction of these classes to G_L lies in L^× (completed) and equals the Kummer class of the corresponding evaluation; for a cusp y and a section s compatible with the canonical integral structure, the restriction corresponds to the first derivative value of θ at y (evaluated with respect to a chosen generator of the cotangent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses systems of N-th roots of local coordinates with specified derivative to produce sections of Dy; the Kummer class of θ^1/N yields the cohomology class. The restriction to G_L is described via the usual H^1(G_L; Z^hat(1)) ≅ (L^×)^hat identification, and at cusps one uses the derivative at the cusp determined by a chosen generator of the cotangent space. Independence of choices (generator/section) up to the expected indeterminacies is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degeneration of Leray–Serre spectral sequences and filtration on H^1
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 7.5(1): the Leray–Serre spectral sequences associated to the filtration of closed subgroups degenerate at E2, yielding a filtration Fil2 ⊂ Fil1 ⊂ Fil0 = H^1(...) on H^1(π; Z_l(1)) with explicit graded quotients: Fil0/Fil1 ≅ Hom((Z_l(1)), Z_l(1)) ≅ Z, Fil1/Fil2 ≅ bZ·log(U), Fil2 ≅ H^1(G_K; Z_l(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identifications use that Z_l(1) has cohomological dimension 1 and Tate-curve/theory of Tate coordinates to identify the elliptic subgroup contribution. The standard isomorphism log(U) is used to view certain subgroups additively. This filtration is fundamental for locating theta classes cohomologically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta class uniqueness and its group action properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 7.5(2): any theta class θ ∈ H^1(π; Z_l(1)) arises from a unique class in H^1(π_filt; Z_l(1)) mapping to the identity homomorphism in the quotient Fil0/Fil1; writing θ + log(O_K) additively, the action of a ∈ 2Z and inversion automorphisms on θ + log(O_K) is given explicitly (formulas involving shifts by multiples of log(U) and log(q_X) plus log(O_K)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely, the subgroup X = 2Z acts by sending θ + log(O_K) to θ + (0)^{2a} log(U) + (0)^{a^2/2} log(q_X) + log(O_K), and inversion automorphisms send θ + log(O_K) to the image with log(U) replaced appropriately. These transformation rules are used to control indeterminacies and equivariance of theta-classes under natural automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anabelian rigidity of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 7.6 (Anabelian Rigidity): Given an isomorphism of abstract topological fundamental groups between two (type (1;1)) log-curves X and yX with stable reduction, (1) the map sends the set of cuspidal decomposition groups and associated Y-objects to the corresponding ones of yX; (2) it induces isomorphisms on the cyclotomic modules Z_l(1) compatible with the natural surjections H^1(G_K; Z_l(1)) → (K^×)^hat and preserves the element 1/2 in the quotients (hence valuations); (3) the induced map on H^1 sends the theta-class subset for X to a yZ-conjugate of the theta-class subset for yX (the yZ-conjugacy arises from choice of component labelled 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is bi-anabelian: the group-theoretic isomorphism reconstructs the geometric data (components, cusps, decomposition groups) and preserves cohomological/torsor structures. Preservation of canonical integral structures of Dy is a key step (one shows the reduction of the structure group of the Sect torsor is determined group-theoretically). The mapping of theta classes is determined up to (K^×)^hat-multiples and then reduced to O_K-multiples by evaluating at cusps and using canonical integral structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard sets of values and standard type for theta classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 7.7: for an etale theta class (and its (Z/2)·(Z/2)-orbit), the corresponding two sets of values at a chosen 4-torsion point zeta are called 'standard sets of values'. There are two values in K^× of maximal valuations in some standard set; if these two maximal-valuation values equal 1 then the theta-class-orbit is called 'of standard type'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition depends on the translation/formula equalities from Lemma 7.4(2) (relations among θ(q^{(0)1}) etc.). The notion of 'standard type' is used to single out theta-classes with distinguished valuation behavior and is the input for rigidity/uniqueness statements that follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant multiple rigidity of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 7.9: (1) an isomorphism of fundamental groups preserves whether a theta-class-orbit is of standard type and this property uniquely determines the collection of classes; (2) such an isomorphism maps standard sets of values for X to standard sets of values for yX under the induced identification K^×^hat ≅ yK^×^hat; (3) if a theta-class-orbit is of standard type and the residue characteristic of K is > 2, then the theta-class-orbit determines an f_{1}g-structure on the (K^×)^hat-torsor at the unique cusp compatible with the canonical integral structure, and this f_{1}g-structure is preserved by the group-theoretic isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a rigidity theorem: after fixing the standard-type condition (and mild residue-characteristic assumption), the indeterminacies of theta-classes reduce to finite predictable ones, enabling reconstruction of discrete torsor reductions (f_{1}g-structures) and values. The proof reduces (3) to (2) and uses elliptic cuspidalisation and preservation of decomposition groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and setup for constructing an l-th root of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7.3 setup: work over a characteristic-0 field K; assume X admits a K-core; let l>2 be a prime; form the natural exact sequences of arithmetic/geometric fundamental groups and consider quotients so that the l-torsion/derived subgroups give a free (Z/lZ)-module of rank 2; choose a quotient Q of the ℓ-adic geometric module onto a rank-1 Z/lZ-module with the restriction Dx -> Q trivial (so the inertia at the cusp maps trivially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions (l>2, choice of quotient Q with prescribed triviality) are used to define and study the l-th root construction of the theta function in the subsequent subsections. The normality of certain subgroups and the injectivity of inertia maps into the quotients are important technical hypotheses in the construction.
